candidate.derivedAnswer: A: When two lines are parallel, alternate interior angles are equal
candidate.answerReason: Alternate interior angles transfer angles B and C to the line through A, where they form a straight angle together with angle BAC.

methods.label: Transfer angles using a parallel line
methods.explanation: Draw \(DE\parallel BC\) through \(A\). Then \(\angle B=\angle BAD\) and \(\angle C=\angle CAE\) (alternate interior angles are equal). Together with \(\angle BAC\), they form a straight angle of \(180^\circ\).
methods.levelReason: Uses grade 7 parallel-line properties to explain the grade 8 triangle angle-sum proof.
